newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen captors want dialogue with French embassy.
newsitem.headline: Yemen captors want dialogue with French embassy.

text.p: Tribesmen holding a French diplomat hostage for the past three days have asked to talk to officials from the French embassy, security sources said on Wednesday.
They said the tribesmen, who kidnapped the diplomat on Monday in Sanaa, made their request to members of other tribes negotiating with them on behalf of the government.
"They said they wanted to open a dialogue with the French embassy," one source said.
French embassy officials in Sanaa refused to comment.
Authorities on Tuesday said security forces would attack homes of the Toaiman tribe if the diplomat was not released by Wednesday midnight (2100 GMT).
The diplomat, who has not been named, is being held in Marib province, 170 km (100 miels) north of Sanaa.

Security officials said earlier they arrested 18 tribe members to put pressure on the abductors and that police and army forces, using light and heavy weapons, were in tight control of the tribe's al-Mahjaza village.

They said the tribe wanted government compensation for losses inflicted on homes, farms, water pumps and wells by floods which killed 65 people in June, more job opportunities and the settlement of a land dispute.
In recent years, tribes in Yemen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped tourists or foreigners for use as bargaining chips.
At least two diplomats, an American and a Saudi ambassador, have been among the kidnap victims.
The tribes' demands have usually involved land or water issues, and have rarely been political. There have been no reported casualties from the abductions.
